== APPRAISAL INSTRUCTIONS (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task D; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §§1-2; APPRAISAL_FORM.md; CODEBOOK.md §8) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:
   - If `Retrieval status` is `not_accessible` (or the paper text below says `[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE]`), you MUST set `paper_read = "not accessible"`, `study_design_identified = "cannot_tell (full text not accessible)"`, `chosen_tool = "cannot_tell"`, `why_tool_chosen = "full text not accessible"`, `overall_rating = "cannot_tell"`, `domain_ratings = []`, all 7 `cross_tool_domains` fields to `"cannot_tell"`, `overall_narrative_summary = "Full text not accessible; no risk-of-bias appraisal performed."`, `where_found_summary = "not accessible"`, and `evidence_quotes = []`. NEVER guess study design or bias ratings from citation/title!

2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

raw_response.chosen_tool: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Low concern / Not applicable to cross-sectional design, though missing administrative data had material handling limitations: districts with 'no record' of surface water deliveries were imputed as receiving zero deliveries rather than excluded or subjected to sensitivity bounds, and Kings County lacked updated LAFCO boundaries (substituted with 2015 DWR boundaries).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern: Neither the irrigation district era/water-right comparisons nor the ID-DAC (n = 97) versus GDC (n = 56) socioeconomic and environmental comparisons adjust for confounding variables such as Valley sub-region and hydrogeology, community population size (mean 9,899 vs. 20,515, p = 0.0035), municipal incorporation or domestic water-system infrastructure, or soil/crop suitability.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Adequate (moderate concern for spatial edge cases): Legal and institutional exposures—district formation eras, pre-1914 senior vs. post-1914 junior appropriative surface water rights, pending petitions, and surface water allocations—were compiled from official administrative registries (SWRCB eWRIMS, USBR contracts, GSPs, AWMPs, county LAFCOs) and verified with district managers; however, Kings County used 2015 DWR boundaries, DAC jurisdiction was assigned via census-place centroids rather than polygon overlap, and agricultural irrigation districts generally do not hold statutory domestic drinking-water mandates.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate-to-high concern: Groundwater reliance is not metered directly but modeled via a residual water-balance deficit combining 2016 Land IQ crop water requirements with 2001–2015 average surface water deliveries (2008–2019 or 2005–2019 for three districts), while imputing 'no record' surface water deliveries as zero. Community outcomes link census-tract-level CalEnviroScreen 4.0 percentiles to DAC census-place centroids, creating ecological/modifiable areal unit measurement error.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak-to-moderate: District groundwater deficit relies on asynchronous land-use (2016) and delivery (2001–2015) inputs, assumes zero lateral groundwater outflow, and treats missing delivery records as zero deliveries. Community drinking-water and groundwater-threat indicators rely on census-tract composite percentiles from CalEnviroScreen 4.0 matched to place centroids rather than direct community water-system or household tap-water measurements.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Moderate concern: No pre-registration or pre-analysis plan is reported. While datasets and R scripts are publicly archived on Dryad and GitHub, the manuscript text omits the total sample size of analyzed irrigation districts, omits sample sizes for two of the five clusters (GDV and CCB), omits dispersion statistics (medians, IQRs, SDs) in Table 1, and omits methodological details of the cluster analysis (clustering algorithm, distance metric, and cluster-count selection criteria).
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate concern: The study covers the full population of agricultural irrigation districts (excluding domestic, municipal, and water conservation agencies) and all DWR-mapped disadvantaged community census places (n = 97 ID-DACs; n = 56 GDCs) on the San Joaquin Valley floor across eight counties, limiting sampling bias, though total district sample size is omitted from the main text and boundary vintages differ for Kings County (2015 DWR vs. updated LAFCO).

domain_ratings.domain_name: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
domain_ratings.justification: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are clearly specified for both analytical units: water agencies on the San Joaquin Valley floor across eight counties that distribute agricultural irrigation water (explicitly excluding water conservation, domestic, and municipal water agencies), and all 2018 DWR-mapped Disadvantaged Community (DAC) census places on the Valley floor classified as within irrigation districts (ID-DACs, n = 97) or outside them in groundwater-dependent communities (GDCs, n = 56). (Note: total irrigation district count N is deferred to supplementary Dryad/supporting tables rather than stated in the main text.)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
domain_ratings.justification: The San Joaquin Valley floor setting (eight counties, hydroclimatic regime, historical California water rights eras since 1887, and SGMA governance context) and study units (irrigation districts across four formation eras and five trait clusters, plus 97 ID-DACs and 56 GDCs) are described in substantial geographic, institutional, and socioeconomic detail, although exact district counts for the overall sample and two clusters (GDV, CCB) are omitted from the main text.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 4–8 of 21], Sections 1.2–1.4 & 2.2; [PDF Page 10–16 of 21], Sections 3.1–3.4, Figs 2–5, Table 1

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
domain_ratings.justification: Legal and institutional exposures (irrigation district boundaries, formation dates/eras, pre-1914 vs. post-1914 surface water rights, and surface water allocations) were derived from authoritative state/federal/local administrative sources (LAFCOs, SWRCB eWRIMS, USBR contractor lists, GSPs, AWMPs) and verified with irrigation district managers. Minor spatial approximations exist because Kings County relied on 2015 DWR boundaries and DAC assignment to irrigation districts used census-place centroids in ArcGIS Pro.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 7–9 of 21], Sections 2.2–2.4; [PDF Page 18 of 21], Acknowledgments

domain_ratings.domain_name: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
domain_ratings.justification: Standardized state administrative and regulatory definitions were used to classify Disadvantaged Communities (2018 DWR DAC Mapping Tool census-place thresholds), agricultural crop categories (2016 DWR-commissioned Land IQ spatial land-use dataset), and historical water management eras (Hanak et al. 2011 periodization and pre-/post-1914 Water Commission Act cutoffs).

The Methods section does not formally identify confounding factors for either the district-era comparisons or the ID-DAC vs. GDC comparisons. Although the Results narratively note co-varying regional characteristics (such as eastern Valley citrus concentration, conveyance access, and the large population size difference between ID-DACs [mean 9,899] and GDCs [mean 20,515]), population size is treated as a parallel outcome in Table 1 rather than identified as a confounder alongside municipal incorporation, domestic water-utility coverage, or local hydrogeology.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 6–10 of 21], Section 2; [PDF Page 13 of 21], Section 3.3, Table 1

domain_ratings.domain_name: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
domain_ratings.justification: No design or analytical strategies (such as multivariable regression, stratification, propensity weighting, spatial fixed effects, or matching) were stated or implemented to control for confounding in either the irrigation district water-balance analysis or the ID-DAC vs. GDC comparison.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 6–10 of 21], Section 2; [PDF Page 13 of 21], Section 3.3, Table 1

domain_ratings.domain_name: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
domain_ratings.justification: While underlying public datasets (Land IQ 2016, WAFR evapotranspiration model, CalEnviroScreen 4.0) are established tools, key operationalization choices create material validity concerns: (1) groundwater reliance is an unvalidated water-budget residual combining asynchronous 2016 crop data with 2001–2015 average surface water deliveries (2008–2019 or 2005–2019 for three districts); (2) districts with 'no record' of surface water deliveries were assumed to receive zero deliveries, risking upward bias in estimated groundwater deficits; and (3) census-tract-level CalEnviroScreen 4.0 percentiles were spatially joined to census-place centroids, introducing ecological measurement error for small DACs.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 8–9 of 21], Sections 2.3–2.4; [PDF Page 12–13 of 21], Fig 4 caption & Table 1

domain_ratings.justification: Statistical analysis has multiple deficiencies: (1) ID-DAC vs. GDC comparisons rely solely on unadjusted bivariate unpaired two-sample Wilcoxon tests across 10 variables with no adjustment for confounding or multiple testing; (2) the authors mischaracterize the Wilcoxon rank-sum test as 'comparing the mean of the variables between the two groups' and report only rounded means (no medians or IQRs) in Table 1 (e.g., PM2.5 shows 92% vs. 92% with p = 0.03291); and (3) the clustering algorithm, distance metric, variable standardization, and cluster-count selection criteria for Fig 5 (as well as inferential tests for era comparisons in Fig 3B) are completely omitted from the Methods text.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 8–10 of 21], Sections 2.2 & 2.4; [PDF Page 13–15 of 21], Sections 3.3–3.4, Table 1 & Fig 5
